points: Gane is the faster, longer fighter with a 7.5-inch reach edge, so his jab should add up damage on Hokit over five rounds.
Hokit has gone the distance only once as a pro, so a five-round pace test favors the champ.
Gane has stopped takedowns from other grappling-heavy opponents and has reportedly worked on his takedown defense.
Prediction markets have Gane at about 64-66%, in line with the 65.9% fair number. The price is a touch better than fair.
research.risk: Hokit's wrestling and chin could turn it into a grind. The edge is only +0.8%, and -189 may be stale.
research.angle: Gane's speed and 7.5-inch reach should carry the champ against a wrestler with cardio questions.
context: Five-round heavyweight title fight at Madison Square Garden. I found no injury or replacement news for either man.
Hokit is 10-0 with a 90% finish rate. His collegiate wrestling is his path, and he has never been finished.
Other shops list Gane at -225 to -245, so -189 is the outlier. Confirm it is still live before betting.
Cappers: Covers (67%) and the CBS panel pick Gane. An MMAmania writer picks Hokit by decision.
